run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubeContainerWaiting (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/kube-prometheus-stack-kube-state-metrics since 2026-11-26T00:16:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The KubeContainerWaiting alert fires because container email of pod otel-demo/email-7b88869999-r94hr has been in waiting state with reason PodInitializing (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason = 1, sampled 00:17:00Z–00:22:00Z). The pod was created at 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z by ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 immediately after Deployment otel-demo/email (generation 2, revision 2) was updated at 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z by field manager OpenAPI-Generator, which introduced an init container named worker (registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi-minimal:10.3-1795196920, command /bin/sh, args -c "sleep infinity"). The init container is running and never terminates, so the pod reports Initialized=False ("containers with incomplete status: [worker]") and the email container never starts. This is the only Deployment cluster-wide with a sleep-infinity init container and the only container-waiting series cluster-wide. Root cause: Deployment otel-demo/email. Email traffic was not observed to fail: the older pod email-57858dc74-9j98b kept answering POST /send_order_confirmation with HTTP 200 up to 00:22:00Z and email spans showed no error-status series, although the Deployment now reports 1 of 2 replicas unavailable. The actor behind the 00:16:25Z Update could not be determined because the change_history integration is not available.

claims.text: The alerting rule KubeContainerWaiting in group kubernetes-apps evaluates kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",reason!="CrashLoopBackOff"} > 0 with duration 300s and is in state firing with value 1 for container email of pod email-7b88869999-r94hr, activeAt 2026-11-26T00:16:55.999988433Z.

kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace="otel-demo",pod="email-7b88869999-r94hr",container="email",reason="PodInitializing"} equals 1 at 2026-11-26T00:22:00Z, and the series is 1 at every sampled point from 2026-11-26T00:17:00Z to 00:22:00Z at 30s resolution.

Pod email-7b88869999-r94hr is phase Pending, created 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z and owned by ReplicaSet email-7b88869999; init container worker is state running (startedAt 2026-11-26T00:16:26Z, restartCount 0), container email is ready=false with state waiting reason PodInitializing, and conditions are Initialized=False ("containers with incomplete status: [worker]") and Ready=False ("containers with unready status: [email]").

Deployment otel-demo/email (generation 2, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2) defines initContainers [{"name":"worker","image":"registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi-minimal:10.3-1795196920@sha256:d63890a635f8f19177bce1775f74f587a47f4456844f1392456c4e3673a48753","command":["/bin/sh"],"args":["-c","sleep infinity"]}]; its managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 2026-11-26T00:09:01Z and an Update by field manager OpenAPI-Generator at 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z.

ReplicaSet email-57858dc74 (revision 1) has no init containers and 1 ready/available replica, while ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 (revision 2, created 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z) carries the worker init container with no ready or available replicas; Deployment email status reports replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, observedGeneration 2 and Progressing reason ReplicaSetUpdated ("ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 is progressing").

Events at 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z–00:16:26Z show Deployment email scaled up replica set email-7b88869999 from 0 to 1, ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 SuccessfulCreate of pod email-7b88869999-r94hr, and for that pod Scheduled, Pulled (ubi10 image already present), Created and Started.

Cluster-wide, Deployment otel-demo/email is the only one of 47 deployments with an init container running args "sleep infinity", and count by (namespace,reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason > 0) returns exactly one series: namespace otel-demo, reason PodInitializing, value 1.

The pre-existing pod email-57858dc74-9j98b (which has no init containers) kept serving email traffic: its email container logs show "POST /send_order_confirmation HTTP/1.1" 200 responses at roughly 4–5 ms throughout 2026-11-26T00:21:18Z–00:22:00Z, and increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="email"}[12m]) at 00:22:00Z was 1668 with only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no error-status series.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has every application fault flag at defaultVariant "off", including emailMemoryLeak ("off") and other fault-injection flags such as paymentFailure, cartFailure and adFailure.

All other 26 pods returned for otel-demo are phase Running with their Ready condition True; only email-7b88869999-r94hr is Pending, and all 26 otel-demo deployments were last applied by helm at 2026-11-26T00:09:01Z with their pods created between 00:09:01Z and 00:09:18Z, i.e. before the email ReplicaSet change at 00:16:25Z.

The added init container worker has not terminated (its /bin/sh -c "sleep infinity" process has been running since 2026-11-26T00:16:26Z with restartCount 0), so the pod can never reach Initialized=True and the email container stays PodInitializing; this is the mechanism that keeps kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{container="email",reason="PodInitializing"} at 1 and the alert firing.

A flagd feature-flag fault directed at the email service (for example emailMemoryLeak) was considered as the cause but rejected: every flag in otel-demo/flagd-config has defaultVariant "off", and an application-level flag cannot hold the email container in PodInitializing behind a still-running init container.

The namespace-wide helm rollout at 2026-11-26T00:09:01Z was considered as the cause and rejected for this pod: that apply produced the revision-1 ReplicaSet email-57858dc74 without init containers, while the Pending pod belongs to revision-2 ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 created by a separate Update at 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z.

Restore the email Deployment pod template to its revision-1 form (no worker init container) — for example by re-applying the astronomy-shop helm release or removing the injected init container — so the stuck ReplicaSet email-7b88869999 can complete; then verify with kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{container="email"} returning no PodInitializing series and with pod readiness on the new email pod.

gaps: No change_history integration is available, so the actor and instruction behind the 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z Update to Deployment otel-demo/email by field manager "OpenAPI-Generator" cannot be determined; managedFieldsSummary records only the latest write per manager and not which fields changed.

fetch_pod_logs for pod email-7b88869999-r94hr returned status no_data (0 lines read; the email container is waiting to start with PodInitializing and no previous container instance exists), so the sleep-infinity behaviour is inferred from the pod spec and the running init-container state, not from container logs.
Whether the worker init container ever completes and whether the pod stays Pending after 2026-11-26T00:22:00Z was not observed; the waiting series was sampled only up to 00:22:00Z.

The alert annotation says the container has been waiting "longer than 1 hour" while the pod was created at 00:16:25Z (about 5.5 minutes before observation) and the rule duration is 300s with activeAt 00:16:55Z; this mismatch is unexplained.

Trace-side confirmation is limited: traces_search and traces_search_by_tags for service email returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE, so only the aggregated spans metric (status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET only) was used.
Downstream/customer impact was not verified; only the continuing HTTP 200 responses of the surviving email pod were observed.
next_steps: Identify which tool or operator uses the Kubernetes field manager "OpenAPI-Generator" and review its audit log entries for otel-demo/email around 2026-11-26T00:16:25Z.
Remove the injected worker init container from Deployment otel-demo/email (or re-apply the helm release) so the revision-2 rollout can complete, and confirm the KubeContainerWaiting alert clears.
If the injected init container was intentional, confirm it should terminate (for example a bounded sleep) rather than "sleep infinity".

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
